title: Separable algebraic tensor finite purely inseparable is a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $k'/k$ be a separable algebraic field extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and let $L/k$ be a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then the ring $L'=k'\otimes_kL$ is a field, and via the ring map $k'\to L'$, $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, $L'$ is a finite purely inseparable field extension of $k'$ with $\dim_{k'}L'=\dim_kL$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QH (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-separable-algebraic, line 47219), proof, first paragraph: 'Then $L' = k' \otimes_k L$ is a field (see material in Fields, Section 037H)'. Section 037H (fields-section-algebraic, fields.tex line 3692) is only a review of definitions and does not state this; the same claim is used in the proofs of Algebra Lemmas 0384 (geometrically normal, line 47062) without further reference. No exact Stacks tag found for the claim.

proof.text: (Realize the tensor as a compositum.) Embed the two extensions in a common algebraic overfield $\Omega$ and write $M=k'L$ for the subfield generated by their images. The multiplication map $\mu:k'\otimes_kL\to M$, $c\otimes x\mapsto cx$, is a $k'$-algebra map. The extensions $k'/k$ and $L/k$ satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-separable-purely-inseparable-linear-disjoint], so $\mu$ is injective. It is also surjective because its image contains $k'$ and $L$, hence the field they generate. Thus $k'\otimes_kL\cong M$; in particular the tensor product is a field.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07QH (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-separable-algebraic), proof, first paragraph; the cited field-theory material is Fields Tags 030K and 037H.

proof.text: (Finite dimension.) If $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ is a $k$-basis of $L$, the standard tensor-basis isomorphism $k'\otimes_kL\cong(k')^d$ sends $1\otimes e_i$ to the $i$-th standard basis vector. Thus $1\otimes e_1,\ldots,1\otimes e_d$ is a $k'$-basis and $\dim_{k'}(k'\otimes_kL)=d=\dim_kL$. Under the isomorphism of Step 1 this gives $[M:k']=[L:k]$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07QH proof, first paragraph, where the base-changed purely inseparable extension is asserted finite; the basis calculation is the elementary tensor-product verification.

proof.text: (Purely inseparable structure.) In characteristic zero, the definition of purely inseparable extension forces $L=k$, so $M=k'$ and the claim is immediate. In characteristic $p>0$, finite-dimensionality gives a common exponent $n$ with $x^{p^n}\in k$ for every $x\in L$ (take a finite generating set and the maximum of their exponents; the Frobenius power of any rational expression then lies in $k$). For $z\in M$, write $z=\sum_i c_i x_i$ with $c_i\in k'$ and $x_i\in L$ using the tensor basis and Step 1. The Frobenius identity in the commutative field $M$ gives $z^{p^n}=\sum_i c_i^{p^n}x_i^{p^n}\in k'$, since $x_i^{p^n}\in k$. Hence every element of $M$ is purely inseparable over $k'$, and $M/k'$ is finite purely inseparable. Transporting this along $k'\otimes_kL\cong M$ proves the assertion for $L'$ and the map $c\mapsto c\otimes1$.
